correctness.rationale: Let X=x(0), B=x(−τ)e^(−a x(−τ)) under a compact translation-invariant law of bounded complete strictly positive Nicholson trajectories. Shift invariance equates the X and x(−τ) marginal laws; stationarity of X and X²/2 gives p EB=δ EX and p E[XB]=δ EX². Their difference gives Cov(X,B)=(δ/p)Var(X). The size-biased measure ν=X μ/EX is well-defined and equivalent to μ, and EB=E[Xe^(−aX)] yields Eν[e^(−aX)]=δ/p=e^(−aK), K=log(p/δ)/a. Strict Jensen for the decreasing convex exponential forces Eν X=EX²/EX≥K; equality implies X constant μ-a.s., shift-invariance at rational times and trajectory continuity force equilibrium K. Cauchy–Schwarz gives Var(B)≥(δ/p)² Var(X). Independently checked exact rational covariance p=8,δ=2,VarX=5/11 giving Cov=5/44. Analytic proofs supply all stationary and equality assertions, not the checker alone.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge PASS for quantitative stationary delayed-recruitment statistical laws. Gurney–Blythe–Nisbet establishes the equation and biology; Berezansky–Braverman–Idels surveys positivity, persistence and oscillation and the theorem that positive solutions eventually staying on one side of K tend to K; Li–Li (2016) full open paper similarly surveys periodicity and stability. The inspected sources do not give size-biased invariant moment floor EX²/EX≥K or exact covariance with the nonlinear delayed input B. The indexed Resultary search found this exact 2026-10-11 result as self-match and otherwise unrelated stationary moment laws of other models. The qualitative oscillation result is acknowledged prior context, not mistaken for the quantitative floor.

value.rationale: The positive equilibrium K is the natural biological population scale, and the delayed nonlinear recruitment B is the model’s actual feedback input. An exact covariance calibration and strict size-biased equilibrium-amplitude moment floor constrain stationary cycles without requiring periodicity, symmetry or ergodicity; these quantitative diagnostics are plausibly reusable to validate deterministic delay simulations and recurring population-law estimates.
